description: Large living room on the Castello side (Paris Review 2008: the castle fills the windows). Pale pink-cream walls, high ceiling, parquet floor with a light rug. Contents seen: upright piano against one wall under framed drawings; white plaster male nude statue on a plinth beside the door to the vestibule; three black-framed glass vitrines in a row against one wall in front of a wooden bookcase (salotto-vetrine); a 19th-c. wooden cabinet full of objects (salotto-wood) with a big TV next to it; a black square coffee table buried under book piles; two white slip-covered armchairs, white sofa(s), one cognac leather club armchair (Eco's interview seat); Tolomeo-type arm floor lamp with parchment shade; a second tall floor lamp; small dark chest/side table by the door.
modelling_note: Box room approx 7 x 6 m, ceiling ~3.5 m. Two windows on the Castello (street) wall. Door to vestibule on the wall where the statue stands; piano on the adjacent wall.

description: Short passage between the salotto door and the long corridor, about 1.5 m wide and 3-4 m long. Left wall: coat hooks/rail with dark overcoats and a hat; beyond them a low white shelf with a small figurine on top and a wall of ~15 framed prints. Right wall: white full-height shelving (Kabbalah/Joyce/esoterica cases B-C-D per Fondazione captions) with a second coat rail with black coats and a hat hung on the shelf end. Facing the walker at the end: the GOSH! pasta-flag artwork with a black twisted mobile hanging in front of it; the walker turns right there into the long corridor. The rare-book room door opens off this passage (coats and white shelves are visible through the rare-room door at film 424 s).
modelling_note: Model as a 1.5 x 3.5 m passage; shelves one side, coats and prints the other; GOSH! on the end wall; 90-degree right turn into the corridor. Rare-room door on the Castello side of the passage.

description: Very long straight corridor (~20 m, ~1.6 m wide) lined with white full-height shelving 11 shelves high on the right-hand side for its whole length (Fondazione bookcase A, 25 bays). In the first third the left wall is shelved too (both sides shelves, film 62-70 s); for the rest the left wall is plain with a row of small framed prints/plexiglass frames. A sliding ladder on a rail and a folding stepladder stand in the corridor. Ceiling with recessed spots; carpeted floor (beige) in the corridor, parquet elsewhere. At the far end a tall French window with vertical iron bars (balcony door), a radiator beneath it, a small metal waste-bin, a wall spotlight above the door.
modelling_note: 20.8 x 1.6 m box; shelves right (25 bays x 0.8 m); left wall: shelves for bays 1-7, prints for the rest; balcony door at the far end; door into the study on the left ~1.5 m before the end.

item: Corridor end lobby by the balcony door
description: The last 2 m of the long corridor: on the left a plain wall with a small speckled grey abstract canvas (~50 x 70 cm) and a switch plate; ahead the French window with vertical bars and a low radiator, a wall lamp above; to the right the last bays of case A. The study door opens on the left just here (Eco turns left at film 82 s / Hq66 329 s).
modelling_note: Place the balcony door on the corridor end wall; door to study on the left wall 1-2 m before it.

description: Large bright room (~14 x 10 m) with white full-height shelving on every wall plus low island bookcases ('pettine e isola') standing in the middle; two white 3-blade ceiling fans; recessed ceiling spots; windows along one long wall (French windows with shutters onto an internal terrace with planters); radiators under the windows; parquet floor. Furniture: L-shaped black desk with computer, printer and phone by the windows; 2-3 black mesh office chairs; a black round pedestal table (~1.4 m dia) at the window end; black leather two-seater sofa; black leather armchair; sliding ladders on rails; black wheeled filing cabinet; white cupboards under the islands; framed caricature portraits of Eco and framed drawings on the pillars between windows; a white door with notes pinned on it on the far wall (where Eco takes a book in the 2015 walk).
modelling_note: Box 14 x 10 m; window wall opposite the corridor door; islands run perpendicular to the long wall; desk in the corner nearest the corridor door by the windows; round table at the far end by the windows.

description: Small high-ceilinged room (~6.5 x 3.6 m; family says originally elliptical) with a French window and wrought-iron balcony looking straight at the corner tower of the Castello Sforzesco. Both long walls: cherry-wood glazed bookcases with a band of drawers/cupboards at waist height, folios and vellum quartos behind glass, mirabilia between the books. Centre: long dark oak table with leather inset and six cane-seat chairs. End wall opposite the balcony: white wall with framed engravings, the door to the vestibule (white shelving and coat hooks visible beyond it). Cognac leather armchair and yellow-shaded floor lamp by the balcony; small round tripod side table; music stand with score and recorder; pendant lamp on a ceiling rail; radiator under the balcony door.
modelling_note: Model as 6.5 x 3.6 m rectangle (or ellipse), balcony on the Castello facade, door to vestibule opposite; cabinets 2.6 m high both long sides; table 2.4 x 1.0 m centred.

item: Internal terrace with planters (outside the study windows)
description: An outdoor terrace/loggia along the study's window wall: a row of terracotta planters with pansies and bergenias on the parapet, ivy climbing the wall, a drainpipe, an air-conditioner unit; through one window the dictionary shelves (LE ROBERT spines = Fondazione Nb 'Dictionaries') and a pendant lamp; through an open French window tall shelves with a sliding ladder and a low bookcase with piles.
modelling_note: Optional exterior: a 1.5 m deep terrace outside the study windows with 6-8 planters; helps locate the study on the courtyard side.

description: Small wrought-iron balcony outside the rare-room French window; view of the round corner tower of the Castello Sforzesco across trees and the road (Renate Ramge looks out at film 306 s).
modelling_note: Balcony 1.2 x 0.6 m with iron railing; skybox with castle tower.

description: Black square coffee table (~1.2 x 1.2 m, low) entirely covered by 10-14 stacks of new books and art catalogues, each 6-15 books, 15-35 cm tall, mostly hardbacks with dust jackets, a few large art books; spines face the sofa. Present in 2015 and 2022. On top of the piles a small orrery-like model (brass rods with small painted spheres). Legible covers in 2015: 'Inventing the Enemy' (Eco), 'Имя розы' (Russian Name of the Rose), 'Une image peut en cacher une autre', 'Italia Vostra'; in 2022 Adelphi/Einaudi paperbacks, 'Privati' (?), Deutschland.
modelling_note: 12 stacks on a 1.2 m black table, heights 15-35 cm, jacketed hardbacks; keep one stack with a red spine on top.

item: Piles on top of the upright piano

Legible: 'Gianni Vattimo', 'Giorgio Morandi - une retrospective', 'Il volto del 900' (Skira), Neil MacGregor 'Vivere con gli dei', Umberto Eco 'Der ewige Faschismus' (2 copies), 'Il nome della rosa', Sofia Bignamini 'I mutanti', 'Versus' journal, Hoepli/Iliprandi 'Note', 'Il Novecento', 'Umberto Eco - A passo di gambero', 'ECO' (Enciclopedia). A crowned wooden Child-Jesus statuette stands on top among the piles.
modelling_note: Piano 1.5 m wide x 1.25 m high; piles on top 0.3-0.4 m; piles on the fold-down music shelf 0.2-0.3 m.

description: The L-shaped black desk and the low black return beside it are heaped with stacks of papers, magazines, folders and books (10-20 stacks, 10-30 cm), plus a telephone, a printer, a desk lamp and the computer monitor; more books lie on the windowsill behind.
modelling_note: Long desk 2.4 x 0.8 m + return 1.2 m; cover 70% of the surface with paper/book stacks 0.1-0.3 m.
